After that decision, I just lost my spark, and my teaching and painting began to feel completely flat.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced episodes of feeling disconnected and losing interest in activities like this before, or is this the first time you've felt this way for an extended period?\n\nPatient: No, I don't recall ever feeling this way before. This is definitely the first time I've experienced these feelings for such a long, extended period.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned this has been going on for eight months, but have you had any periods within those eight months where your mood or interest in activities improved for a little while, or has it been consistently this way the entire time?\n\nPatient: It has been consistently this way the entire time without any real breaks or periods of improvement. That heavy, flat feeling has been there pretty much every single day, and it hasn't really lifted even for a moment.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any changes in your appetite, sleep patterns, or energy levels since you started feeling this way, and if so, how have they changed?\n\nPatient: Lately, my sleep is awful—I lie awake replaying work emails or wake up around 3 or 4 AM with this heavy anxiety and can't fall back asleep, leaving me totally exhausted and foggy. I also barely have the energy to keep up with my normal tasks, though I haven't noticed any major changes in my appetite.\n\nDoctor: Do you often find yourself feeling guilty, worthless, or having negative thoughts about yourself since you started feeling disconnected from your classes and art?\n\nPatient: Yes, I feel that way constantly. Ever since I was passed over for the promotion, I feel like a complete fraud and a disappointment to my students, my department, and even my husband. It stays quite steady, though some days can feel worse than others, especially after a long, unproductive evening at my desk.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned that things you used to enjoy feel flat and pointless, but have you experienced any pleasure or interest in social activities or being around other people during these eight months?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't found any pleasure in being around people either, and I've ended up backing out of art meet-ups, canceling student activities, and avoiding department events. I've also become really withdrawn at home, and my husband has had to take over most of our household tasks because I just don't have the energy. However, these are just passive thoughts, and I have absolutely no plans or intentions to act on them.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about these passive thoughts of not wanting to wake up or slip away, and have you ever found yourself wishing you could escape your current situation in any way?\n\nPatient: Yes, it really feels like a passive desire to escape the constant pressure and disappointment. On those worst nights at my desk, I just think it would be easier if I didn't wake up so no one would have to deal with me anymore. But I've never made a plan or had any intention of acting on it; it's just a wish for the heavy feeling to stop.\n\nDoctor: You've described a consistent and significant impact on your daily life and activities due to your depressive symptoms, but can you clarify if there are any specific aspects of your life, such as work or relationships, where you feel you're still managing to function relatively normally despite your symptoms?\n\nPatient: Honestly, it feels like almost every area of my life is heavily impacted, and nothing feels normal or functional anymore. Before this, I used to handle a heavy teaching load and creative projects with genuine excitement, but now I feel completely flat and overwhelmed by even minor stressors. Reply naturally in English as the Patient to the last Doctor utterance.\nAnswer only the question, in 2–3 sentences maximum.\n\n[Dialogue]\nDoctor: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?\n\nPatient: I don’t enjoy my classes or my art anymore, and the things that used to excite me just feel flat and pointless. I just feel completely disconnected from everything that used to bring me joy, and I don't know how to fix it.\n\nDoctor: How long have you been feeling this way, and was there a specific event or time when you noticed your enjoyment in classes and art starting to fade?\n\nPatient: These feelings have been going on steadily for about eight months now. It really started when I was passed over for a long-anticipated promotion to a tenure-track position in my department. After that decision, I just lost my spark, and my teaching and painting began to feel completely flat.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced episodes of feeling disconnected and losing interest in activities like this before, or is this the first time you've felt this way for an extended period?\n\nPatient: No, I don't recall ever feeling this way before. This is definitely the first time I've experienced these feelings for such a long, extended period.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned this has been going on for eight months, but have you had any periods within those eight months where your mood or interest in activities improved for a little while, or has it been consistently this way the entire time?\n\nPatient: It has been consistently this way the entire time without any real breaks or periods of improvement. That heavy, flat feeling has been there pretty much every single day, and it hasn't really lifted even for a moment.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any changes in your appetite, sleep patterns, or energy levels since you started feeling this way, and if so, how have they changed?\n\nPatient: Lately, my sleep is awful—I lie awake replaying work emails or wake up around 3 or 4 AM with this heavy anxiety and can't fall back asleep, leaving me totally exhausted and foggy. I also barely have the energy to keep up with my normal tasks, though I haven't noticed any major changes in my appetite.\n\nDoctor: Do you often find yourself feeling guilty, worthless, or having negative thoughts about yourself since you started feeling disconnected from your classes and art?\n\nPatient: Yes, I feel that way constantly. Ever since I was passed over for the promotion, I feel like a complete fraud and a disappointment to my students, my department, and even my husband. I constantly obsess over every small mistake I make as proof that I'm incompetent and don't deserve the job I have.\n\nDoctor: Have you had any previous episodes of depression that lasted for a shorter period, or is this the first episode you've experienced, and if so, do you think this episode might be related to the specific event of being passed over for the promotion?\n\nPatient: I have never experienced anything like this before, so this is definitely the first time I've ever felt this way. I absolutely believe it is related to being passed over for the promotion, as these heavy feelings started the exact moment that happened.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned this is your first episode of feeling this way, but considering the duration and your symptoms, can you tell me if you've had any periods of hypomanic or manic episodes in the past, where you felt abnormally happy, energetic, or irritable for a period of time?\n\nPatient: No, I've never experienced anything like that. I have never had periods of feeling abnormally energetic, hyperactive, or euphoric in the past.\n\nDoctor: Given that you've had a consistent, unrelenting period of depressive symptoms for eight months without any prior episodes, and considering the significant impact of the job promotion event, can you describe how you would characterize the intensity of your depressive symptoms over this period, and have you noticed any subtle variations in how they affect you from one month to another?\n\nPatient: The intensity has been a moderate but very heavy and constant fog that just doesn't lift, and it hasn't really changed from month to month. It stays quite steady, though some days can feel worse than others, especially after a long, unproductive evening at my desk.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned that things you used to enjoy feel flat and pointless, but have you experienced any pleasure or interest in social activities or being around other people during these eight months?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't found any pleasure in being around people either, and I've ended up backing out of art meet-ups, canceling student activities, and avoiding department events. I've also become really withdrawn at home, and my husband has had to take over most of our household tasks because I just don't have the energy. Everything just feels too flat and exhausting.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any thoughts of self-harm, suicidal ideation, or feelings that life is not worth living during this period of feeling disconnected and depressed?\n\nPatient: On my worst days, particularly after a long and unproductive evening at my desk, I do catch myself thinking it would be easier if I just didn't wake up or could quietly slip away. However, these are just passive thoughts, and I have absolutely no plans or intentions to act on them.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about these passive thoughts of not wanting to wake up or slip away, and have you ever found yourself wishing you could escape your current situation in any way?\n\nPatient: Yes, it really feels like a passive desire to escape the constant pressure and disappointment. On those worst nights at my desk, I just think it would be easier if I didn't wake up so no one would have to deal with me anymore. But I've never made a plan or had any intention of acting on it; it's just a wish for the heavy feeling to stop.\n\nDoctor: You've described a consistent and significant impact on your daily life and activities due to your depressive symptoms, but can you clarify if there are any specific aspects of your life, such as work or relationships, where you feel you're still managing to function relatively normally despite your symptoms?\n\nPatient: Honestly, it feels like almost every area of my life is heavily impacted, and nothing feels normal or functional anymore. While I still drag myself to work and go through the motions of teaching because I have to, I've fallen way behind on grading and have had to cancel student activities. Between that and my husband having to take over most of the household chores, both my professional and personal lives are suffering significantly.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned feeling exhausted and having no energy, can you tell me more about how this has affected your daily activities and ability to complete tasks?\n\nPatient: The constant exhaustion has made it incredibly hard to keep up, causing me to fall behind on grading and cancel my student art activities. I've also been avoiding department events entirely because I just don't have the energy to participate. At home, my husband has had to take over most of the household chores because I'm simply too drained and unmotivated to do them.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your symptoms have affected your ability to function in your daily life, particularly in terms of work and relationships, and have you noticed any differences in how you're able to cope with stressful situations compared to before you started feeling this way?\n\nPatient: My daily functioning is severely impacted; I've fallen behind on grading, canceled student activities, and my husband has had to take over the household chores because I'm so drained. Before this, I used to handle a heavy teaching load and creative projects with genuine excitement, but now I feel completely flat and overwhelmed by even minor stressors. It is a night-and-day difference in my ability to cope compared to how I used to be.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned that things you used to enjoy feel flat and pointless, but have you experienced any moments or situations where you felt a slight return of interest or pleasure in any activities, no matter how small, over the past eight months?\n\nPatient: No, unfortunately, there really haven't been any moments where that pleasure has returned. Even when something objectively good happens—like a student thanking me or a painting actually turning out well—the joy just isn't there. I'm just left with this heavy, hollow sadness and a flatness that doesn't lift.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any loss of interest in activities that you normally enjoy, such as hobbies or spending time with friends and family, and if so, can you describe how that has affected your daily life?\n\nPatient: Yes, I've lost all interest in painting, planning new assignments, and going to art meet-ups; when I try to start, I just end up staring at a blank canvas because it all feels so flat. This has led me to cancel student art activities and completely avoid department events. At home, it's gotten to the point where my husband has had to take over almost all of our household chores because I simply lack the energy and motivation to keep up.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned losing interest in activities you used to enjoy, but have you experienced any physical symptoms such as changes in appetite or weight, or any other somatic symptoms alongside your feelings of disconnection and depression?\n\nPatient: I haven't noticed any significant changes in my appetite or weight, but my sleep has been a major physical struggle. I often lie awake for hours replaying work emails in my head, or I wake up around 3 or 4 in the morning with a heavy, anxious feeling and can't fall back asleep. This leaves me dragging myself through my classes feeling completely exhausted and foggy.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how often you experience this heavy, anxious feeling that wakes you up at 3 or 4 in the morning, and does it occur at any other times of the day as well?\n\nPatient: Lately, waking up at 3 or 4 in the morning with that anxious, heavy feeling has been happening almost every single night. A similar heavy, hollow sadness persists throughout the day as well, feeling like a gray film over everything that doesn't really lift even when I am at work.\n\nDoctor: You've had a consistent depressive episode for eight months without any prior episodes, but can you clarify if you've experienced any brief periods, even just a few days, where your symptoms seemed to improve or lighten, even if they returned afterwards?\n\nPatient: No, there haven't been any breaks or lighter periods at all. This heavy, flat feeling has been there pretty much constantly every single day for the past eight months without lifting, even for a few days. It has just been completely steady and continuous.\n\nDoctor: Do you feel that your depression is worse in the morning, and does it improve at all as the day goes on?"

At home, my husband has had to take over most of the household chores because I'm simply too drained and unmotivated to do them.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your symptoms have affected your ability to function in your daily life, particularly in terms of work and relationships, and have you noticed any differences in how you're able to cope with stressful situations compared to before you started feeling this way?\n\nPatient: My daily functioning is severely impacted; I've fallen behind on grading, canceled student activities, and my husband has had to take over the household chores because I'm so drained. Before this, I used to handle a heavy teaching load and creative projects with genuine excitement, but now I feel completely flat and overwhelmed by even minor stressors. It is a night-and-day difference in my ability to cope compared to how I used to be.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned that things you used to enjoy feel flat and pointless, but have you experienced any moments or situations where you felt a slight return of interest or pleasure in any activities, no matter how small, over the past eight months?\n\nPatient: No, unfortunately, there really haven't been any moments where that pleasure has returned. Even when something objectively good happens—like a student thanking me or a painting actually turning out well—the joy just isn't there. I'm just left with this heavy, hollow sadness and a flatness that doesn't lift.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any loss of interest in activities that you normally enjoy, such as hobbies or spending time with friends and family, and if so, can you describe how that has affected your daily life?\n\nPatient: Yes, I've lost all interest in painting, planning new assignments, and going to art meet-ups; when I try to start, I just end up staring at a blank canvas because it all feels so flat. This has led me to cancel student art activities and completely avoid department events. At home, it's gotten to the point where my husband has had to take over almost all of our household chores because I simply lack the energy and motivation to keep up.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned losing interest in activities you used to enjoy, but have you experienced any physical symptoms such as changes in appetite or weight, or any other somatic symptoms alongside your feelings of disconnection and depression?\n\nPatient: I haven't noticed any significant changes in my appetite or weight, but my sleep has been a major physical struggle. This heavy, flat feeling has been there pretty much constantly every single day for the past eight months without lifting, even for a few days.
